A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViT-P work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material. v1 Appendix A.1–A.4 corresponds to v2 Sections 6–9; no material gap prevents comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ViT-P segmentation experiments, ablations and appendix comparisons, including results on ADE20K, Cityscapes and COCO.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, upper-bound analysis and mask-versus-point prompting comparison.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the reported box-pretraining procedure from sampling labeled points inside boxes to directly supplying [x,y,w,h] coordinates, followed by point fine-tuning using [x,y,0,0]. This is a localized input/training adaptation; the transformer classifier and geometric score fusion remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The same segmentation tasks and dataset coverage are retained, including ADE20K, Cityscapes, COCO, COCO-Stuff-164K and Objects365 pretraining. Changing how box annotations are encoded does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the supplementary comparisons. In particular, the MAFT comparison with CLIP and DINOv2 remains in v1 Table 9 and v2 Table 6.

E3.justification: The reported preparation of Objects365 pretraining examples changes from within-box point sampling to direct box-coordinate inputs, with subsequent point fine-tuning specified in Section 3.4. Metrics, benchmark settings and Section 4.2 training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The point-count, point-selection, backbone and annotation ablations are retained as v2 Table 4a–d. The appendix upper-bound and prompting analyses and all qualitative examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimates for the experiments.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results are unchanged across Tables 1–3, the matched ablation tables and the appendix comparisons. Figures retain identical result imagery. No new result separately evaluates the revised box-input procedure.

T1.justification: The token-concatenation and geometric-fusion equations retain the same mathematics. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs, and v2 adds no formal result, assumption or derivation; its coordinate-encoding revision concerns the training procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: decoupled mask generation and classification, adaptation of pretrained transformers, inexpensive annotation use and the same benchmark-performance claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds the rationale that box-coordinate pretraining teaches object location and scale, with zero-size boxes maintaining input consistency during point fine-tuning. The result interpretations and limitations concerning marginal instance/panoptic gains and dependence on score ensembling are retained.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents four-coordinate box inputs, zero-padding of point coordinates and the box-pretraining-to-point-fine-tuning sequence. Hardware, optimizer, learning rate, crop sizes, training epochs and the code/model access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 57 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Reference renumbering, expanded author names and bibliography formatting do not change the cited literature.

P1.justification: v2 revises the box-training paragraphs and replaces inconsistent central-point descriptions with highest-value-point or general point terminology. Appendix subsections become Sections 6–9, while most prose and the narrative sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. v1 Tables 4–7 become four panels of v2 Table 4, and the supplementary tables move together onto a separate page. The six underlying figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity by aligning point-selection terminology with the highest-value rule already used in v1's implementation and ablation. It also makes the revised box-input and point-fine-tuning formats explicit. These are limited documentation gains: empirical evidence is unchanged, and no experiment compares the revised box-pretraining procedure with the earlier description.
